In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the SQL Profiler save and load functions in the PEM web application do not keep the client-supplied file name inside the user's storage directory. A user with the SQL Profiler role (pem_comp_sqlprofiler) can read JSON files, and overwrite files that the PEM web server account can write, outside their own storage directory. Overwriting the PEM web application's configuration database stops the web console for all users.
From PEM 10.6.1, the SQL Profiler only reads and writes files inside the user's storage directory.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), multi-factor authentication (MFA) is not enforced on the PEM web application's own routes. An attacker who knows the password of a user who has enrolled a second factor can skip the second factor and call PEM's pages and APIs directly, with that user's permissions. A similar issue in pgAdmin 4 was assigned CVE-2024-4215.
From PEM 10.6.1, every authenticated PEM route requires a completed MFA check.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), several SECURITY DEFINER functions in the pem schema of the PEM backend database are owned by a superuser but do not set a safe search_path. Any PEM user who can connect to the PEM backend database can create objects that these functions use in place of the intended ones, and so run arbitrary SQL with superuser privileges. Temporary objects can be used for this on every supported PostgreSQL version, and objects in the public schema on PostgreSQL 14 backends and backends upgraded from PostgreSQL 14.
From PEM 10.6.1, these functions run with a fixed search_path.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the row-level security policies on pem.job and pem.jobstep that apply to PEM agents do not limit an agent to its own jobs. An attacker who controls one monitored host, and so its PEM agent certificate, can create, change or delete jobs for every other agent, including the agent on the PEM server. Agents run SQL job steps with the database credentials of the server they monitor, and shell job steps where batch jobs are enabled, so compromising one monitored host can give superuser SQL access to every monitored database and to the PEM backend.
From PEM 10.6.1, PEM agents can no longer create jobs or change job definitions or job steps.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the pem_agent role, which every PEM agent login inherits, is a member of the PostgreSQL pg_read_server_files and pg_write_server_files roles on the PEM backend database. An attacker who controls any monitored host, and so its PEM agent certificate, can read and write files on the PEM server host as the postgres operating system user. This includes the PEM certificate authority key, which lets the attacker issue certificates for other agents and act as them.
From PEM 10.6.1, PEM agents no longer hold these roles.

Poste.io is vulnerable to remote code execution in DMARC report processing. Email sent to dmarc-reports@<domain> is saved without sender verification. Script that runs as root unpacks the attachments using unsafe shell commands, allowing command injection through crafted attachments (e.g. file names or archive contents). A remote unauthenticated attacker who can send an email to the server's port 25 can execute arbitrary commands as root within the Poste.io container.


This issue was fixed in version 2.5.22.

Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix_live_view allows an authenticated user to mount a router-mounted LiveView without the on_mount hooks of its live_session via a phx_join message that carries neither a "url" nor a "redirect" key.

The catch-all clause of the private Phoenix.LiveView.Channel.authorize_session/3 in lib/phoenix_live_view/channel.ex accepts a join without a URL for any session, including a root LiveView mounted at the router. The channel then mounts the LiveView with no route, and only a route adds the live_session hooks to the mount lifecycle. Checks that those hooks perform on the connected mount do not run, and event checks that they attach through attach_hook/4 are never attached. The attacker needs a valid session token for the LiveView, which only the HTTP render issues, after the hooks pass there. on_mount hooks declared in the LiveView module still run.

This issue affects phoenix_live_view: from 0.16.0 before 1.0.20, from 1.1.0-rc.0 before 1.1.34, and from 1.2.0-rc.0 before 1.2.14.

A Path Traversal vulnerability in workspace directory handling and Git integration in Google Cloud Dataform, BigQuery Studio and Colab Enterprise on Google Cloud Platform allows an authenticated remote attacker to read private files and create arbitrary files across tenant repositories using crafted workspace operations and Git integration requests.


This vulnerability was patched on 10 October 2026, and no customer action is needed.

The BuddyBoss Addons plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in versions up to, and including, 1.2.1. This is due to the Social Login REST endpoint trusting unverified Apple and Facebook identity-token claims and linking an attacker-controlled provider identifier to an existing WordPress user selected by the token’s email claim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know a user’s email address to associate their provider identity with that account, including administrator accounts, and subsequently authenticate as the victim. Successful exploitation requires the BuddyBoss Platform plugin to be installed and active, with the Social Login module and selected provider enabled and configured. On sites with the separate BuddyBoss App JWT component, the vulnerable REST request can return an application token immediately.

Exposure of sensitive system information to an unauthorized control sphere vulnerability in Tegsoft Yönetim ve Bilişim Hizmetleri Tic. Ltd. Şti. Tegsoft İletişim Merkezi allows Query System for Information.

This issue affects Tegsoft İletişim Merkezi: before latest-202611161510.

Unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability in Tegsoft Yönetim ve Bilişim Hizmetleri Tic. Ltd. Şti. Tegsoft Contact Center allows Upload a Web Shell to a Web Server.

This issue affects Tegsoft Contact Center: before latest-202611161510.

A vulnerability was found in antirez gguf-tools up to fdfafbed766db0a1e9019b07994cd88f133d1aab. The impacted element is the function gguf_get_tensor of the file gguflib.c of the component GGUF Parser. The manipulation of the argument offset/alignment results in out-of-bounds read. The attack can be launched remotely. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

A vulnerability was found in erupts erupt up to 2.0.2. This impacts the function EruptUserController.createCode of the file erupt-upms/src/main/java/xyz/erupt/upms/controller/EruptUserController.java of the component UPMS CAPTCHA Endpoint. Performing a manipulation of the argument height results in uncontrolled memory allocation. The attack may be initiated remotely. Upgrading to version 2.0.3 will fix this issue. The patch is named fc59a6eece991ff5aced363243d0b2d14f73ed95. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Brainstorm Force SureCart surecart allows Stored XSS.This issue affects SureCart: from n/a through 4.13.0.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in miniOrange miniOrange's Google Authenticator miniorange-2-factor-authentication allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects miniOrange's Google Authenticator: from n/a through 6.6.0.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in Tribulant Software Newsletters newsletters-lite allows SQL Injection.This issue affects Newsletters: from n/a through 4.18.2.
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Tribulant Software Newsletters newsletters-lite allows Object Injection.This issue affects Newsletters: from n/a through 4.18.2.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Gemini Labs Site Reviews site-reviews allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Site Reviews: from n/a through 8.3.7.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Tomdever wpForo Forum wpforo allows Stored XSS.This issue affects wpForo Forum: from n/a through 3.2.4.

Mongoose Embedded Web Server / Networking Library before 7.24 contains a WebSocket fragmentation validation vulnerability that allows remote attackers to spoof message metadata by sending a single CONTINUATION frame with FIN=1 as the first data frame instead of a required TEXT/BINARY start frame, violating RFC 6455 sequencing rules. Attackers can craft this malformed frame to make mg_ws_cb() in src/ws.c misinterpret the first byte of payload as saved FIN/opcode flags, causing the application to receive a dispatched MG_EV_WS_MSG event with attacker-controlled flags and data truncated by one byte without closing the connection.

llama.cpp b11003 before b12556 contains an integer overflow in the hrm_text loader load_arch_hparams() that allows attackers to bypass the block count check using crafted GGUF metadata. Attackers can supply a GGUF model whose layer factors wrap modulo 2^32, causing load_arch_tensors() to write tensor pointers past model.layers, corrupting heap memory and potentially enabling code execution.

C-Blosc2 before 3.4.1 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds read vulnerability in frame_decompress_chunk() because sparse frame chunk cbytes are not checked against the actual chunk file size. Attackers can supply a sparse frame directory with a truncated or crafted chunk file to crash applications or leak adjacent heap memory into decompressed output.

diffpy.structure before 3.5.1 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run Python code by supplying crafted CIF symmetry operations passed to eval() in get_symop(). Attackers can embed expressions in the _space_group_symop_operation_xyz or _symmetry_equiv_pos_as_xyz loop to execute code with victim privileges when the CIF file is parsed locally.

The targets R package before 1.12.1 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run arbitrary R code by planting format functions in the data store metadata file. Attackers can supply a crafted _targets data store whose custom format or CAS repository functions are passed to eval(parse()), executing code when victims call tar_read(), tar_load() or tar_workspace().

request-filtering-agent before 3.2.2 contains a server-side request forgery filter bypass because address validation in src/request-filtering-agent.ts treats IPv4-compatible IPv6 addresses in the ::/96 range as public unicast. Attackers controlling a fetched URL can use addresses like ::7f00:1 or ::a9fe:a9fe to reach loopback or link-local services, including cloud metadata endpoints.

Hanko before 3.2.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability in Saml.IsAllowedRedirect that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass the redirect allowlist by appending attacker-controlled domain suffixes to allowed hostnames. Attackers can lure victims through a crafted /saml/auth login link to capture the one-time hanko_token and redeem it without PKCE to hijack the victim's session.

Penpot 2.18.0 before 2.18.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with edit rights to bypass the sanitize-svg-element blocklist using namespace-prefixed SVG elements. Attackers can upload SVGs containing elements like x:script or attributes like x:onload, which are served inline as image/svg+xml to run JavaScript in victims' Penpot sessions.

Open5GS AMF through 2.8.0 contains a resource leak vulnerability that allows authenticated UEs to exhaust the session pool by triggering failed DNN or S-NSSAI validation. Attackers can repeat PDU Session Establishment Requests with different PDU Session Identity values, leaving stale amf_sess contexts that degrade service for other subscribers.

free5GC PCF through 1.4.6 contains a resource leak in postAppSessCtxProcedure that leaves PCC rules and QoS data in the SM policy decision after rejected Npcf_PolicyAuthorization create requests. Authenticated AFs knowing an active PDU session's UE address can send repeated failing requests with distinct AF application identifiers to grow PCF memory and pollute policy sent to the SMF.

free5GC SMF through 1.4.6 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease that orphans SM contexts and UE IP addresses when PFCP session deletion fails. Attackers can send repeated PDU session establishment requests reusing an existing SUPI and PDU Session ID during PFCP deletion failures to exhaust the DNN's UE IP pool.

free5GC SMF through 1.4.6 contains a resource leak vulnerability in HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate that leaves SM contexts unreleased when UDM access token retrieval fails. Attackers can trigger repeated PDU session establishment attempts while the NRF is unreachable, causing empty 200 responses and persistent SMF memory growth.

free5GC SMF through 1.4.6 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability because sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept returns early without calling RemoveSMContextFromAllNF on failures. Authenticated UEs repeatedly establishing PDU sessions during NRF or AMF failures leak SM contexts, UE IP addresses and TEIDs, exhausting the DNN IP pool.

A vulnerability was identified in OpenZipkin Zipkin 3.6.1. This affects the function UnzippingBytesRequestConverter.convertRequest of the file zipkin-server/src/main/java/zipkin2/server/internal/ZipkinHttpCollector.java of the component HTTP Collector. Such manipulation leads to highly compressed data. The attack can be executed remotely. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

A vulnerability was determined in tianshiyeben wgcloud up to 4.0.1. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file AgentController.java of the component minTask Endpoint. Executing a manipulation can lead to allocation of resources. The attack can be executed remotely.

A weakness has been identified in PowerJob up to 5.1.7. This affects the function CustomHttpServletRequestWrapper of the file powerjob-server/powerjob-server-starter/src/main/java/tech/powerjob/server/config/CachingRequestBodyFilter.java of the component CachingRequestBodyFilter. Executing a manipulation can lead to denial of service. It is possible to launch the attack remotely.
A bug caused room permissions to leak into the world permissions of the acting user during certain actions.

Joomla Extension - solidres.com - Unauthenticated stored XSS through guest reservation details in Solidres extension 1.0.0-3.4.1, 4.0.0-4.6.0 - The customer details layout of the administrator reservation view printed guest-supplied booking details, including the email and phone number inside mailto: and tel: links, without escaping, allowing unauthenticated guests to inject HTML attributes and script. Sites using the Custom Fields, Hub or Experience add-ons also need to update them to Custom Fields 2.0.3, Hub 2.5.0 and Experience 2.5.0.

Joomla Extension - phoca.cz - Stored XSS through author website in frontend upload in Phoca Download extension 3.0.6-6.1.6 - The author website field of the frontend upload form was validated with an overly permissive URL check and rendered without escaping, allowing users with frontend upload permission to inject HTML attributes into the file and category views.

Joomla Extension - joomlatools.com - Server-side request forgery in URL uploads in DOCman extension < 6.2.2 - The URL proxy and URL upload features were available to users below manager level and fetched arbitrary addresses, allowing server-side requests to internal or private network resources.

Joomla Extension - joomlatools.com - Local file read through remote document links in DOCman extension < 6.2.2 - Remote document links accepted the file:// scheme, allowing users with permission to create or edit documents to download arbitrary local files from the server, such as the Joomla configuration file.

Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel vulnerability in miniOrange miniorange otp verification miniorange-otp-verification allows Authentication Abuse.This issue affects miniorange otp verification: from n/a through 5.6.1.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in RomanCode MapSVG mapsvg-lite-interactive-vector-maps allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects MapSVG: from n/a through 9.0.5.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Elementor Elementor Website Builder elementor allows Reflected XSS.This issue affects Elementor Website Builder: from n/a through 4.4.0.

Net::DNS uses a 16-bit query ID to match responses to the corresponding requests.  In versions up to and including 1.57, the ID is obtained from Perl's built-in rand() function.  An attacker that can observe the sequence of query IDs is able to expose the internal state of the PNRG and hence predict query IDs before they are transmitted.  The victim Net::DNS instance is then exposed to forged responses injected by the attacker.  Note that the deduplication cache in 1.57 has no impact on the feasibility of this attack.

A vulnerability was found in hiparker opsli-boot up to 2.2.1. This affects the function getInputStream of the file opsli-plugins/opsli-plugins-waf/src/main/java/org/opsli/plugins/waf/servlet/WafHttpServletRequestWrapper.java of the component WAF Plugin. The manipulation results in denial of service. The attack can be executed remotely.

A vulnerability was detected in itsourcecode Banking Management System 1.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file manage_donation.php of the component Donor Management. The manipulation of the argument ID results in sql injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit is now public and may be used.

The Seraphinite Accelerator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.31 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has previously enabled the 'Enable logging' and 'HTTP trace' diagnostic options in the plugin's Advanced → Debug settings, both of which are disabled by default.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in myCred myCred mycred allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects myCred: from n/a through 4.0.3.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Liquid Web / StellarWP Gutenberg Blocks by Kadence Blocks kadence-blocks allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Gutenberg Blocks by Kadence Blocks: from n/a through 3.9.1.1.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in PublishPress PublishPress Permissions press-permit-core allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects PublishPress Permissions: from n/a through 5.0.1.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in weDevs Dokan dokan-lite allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Dokan: from n/a through 5.3.4.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in myCred myCred mycred allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects myCred: from n/a through 4.0.3.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Brainstorm Force Spectra ultimate-addons-for-gutenberg allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Spectra: from n/a through 2.20.6.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Magepeople inc. Taxi Booking Manager for WooCommerce ecab-taxi-booking-manager allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Taxi Booking Manager for WooCommerce: from n/a through 2.2.10.

Our payment integration with Stripe did not properly validate payment status responses. An attacker could use a successful payment status response from one payment and supply it to the system for a different payment, gaining access to multiple valid tickets with only one payment. However, the attack requires knowledge of a valid charge ID from the same event which we believe is usually not exposed to users.




To simplify attack surface, the fix removes support for incoming webhooks regarding payments created through Stripe's old "source" API. pretix stopped creating payments using this API in 2024.1 for most payment methods and in 2024.9 for all payment methods.

When a scheduled export is copied, the permissions of the original export's owner are used when running the export. This allows users to create exports with data they usually shouldn't be able to see, but only within events they already have permissions to.

A legacy code path allowed users to craft requests to a ticket shop that bypass some validation steps for the selected products. In consequence, this could lead to an attacker purchasing products that are in fact sold out.

pretix offloads certain processes to background tasks that are run by a different server to avoid HTTP workers being clogged with processes that take longer than a usual web request. The browser periodically polls the server to see if the task is already finished using a UUID-shaped task ID. Once the task is completed, pretix resumes to the next step of the operation based on the result of the task. The system does however not check if the result stems from the correct type of task. Therefore, an attacker can supply the UUID of a task of a different type and pretix will continue with the result from the wrong task. In most cases, this will just result in an error because the return types do not match up, but in some cases this can be abused to extract objects the attacker usually should not see. Specifically, a vector was discovered that allowed to abuse this for unauthorized access to other people's ticket purchases. The attacker can, however, not control which purchases they get access to.

When configuring a device to use the security profile "pretixSCAN (kiosk mode, no order sync, no search)", the API search endpoint introduced in pretix 4.12 was not blocked correctly. This theoretically allows these devices to perform searches for orders even if that was not intended. If the device is in kiosk mode, the search button will still be hidden from users.

The fix for CVE-2026-127174 published in 2026.9.2 is incomplete: When expanding an export from "some events" to "all events", it is checked that the acting user is part of a team with permission to all events, but this check is not correctly bound to the organizer and could also be passed through permissions on a different organizer.

When a ticket holder opens the ticket page of a ticket that is an add-on (possible since 2026.9) the HTML content of the page contains the secret link to the parent product, creating a potential data leak. Under different specific conditions, when a ticket contains user-uploaded files in response to a question, the page can even contain the secret link to the entire order.

A stored XSS in pretix-adyen has been discovered where an attacker could configure his own ticket shop in a way that API calls are not made to Adyen, but an attacker-controlled server. Results of these API calls would then be embedded in a part of the shop without proper escaping, leading to full XSS including potential session takeover.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Omnisend Newsletters, Email Marketing, SMS and Popups by Omnisend omnisend allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Newsletters, Email Marketing, SMS and Popups by Omnisend: from n/a through 1.9.1.

The Simple Membership WP user Import plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in all versions up to, and including, 1.9.2 This is due to missing or incorrect nonce validation on the add function. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to import arbitrary WordPress users into Simple Membership and modify their WordPress role via the plugin's membership-level-to-role mapping via a forged request granted they can trick a site administrator into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Optimole – Optimize Images | Convert WebP & AVIF | CDN & Lazy Load | Image Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.19 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the AMP plugin to be active in Transitional or Standard template mode, and comments must be open on the target post, which is the WordPress default.

Authenticated users can bypass normal controls on the reading and writing of workflow execution results. This allows any authenticated user to read or modify any other user's workflow execution results.



This issue affects Apache Texera (incubating): from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue.

flowintel contains multiple related flaws that allow an authenticated attacker to inject arbitrary HTML or script into pages viewed by other users.

- Timeline rendering: the timeline library's autolinking feature rewrote already-sanitised case notes and imported MISP attribute values into generated HTML link elements. Crafted text containing quote characters could break out of the generated attribute context, altering the surrounding markup and enabling script execution in the victim's browser.

- Search highlighting: the highlight injection logic used a regular expression to locate text between angle brackets and spliced <mark> elements into the resulting string. Because the pattern could match inside HTML attribute values, the rewrite could corrupt or inject content into attributes of already-sanitised markup, again leading to DOM-based cross-site scripting.

- Content-Type confusion: three analyser selection endpoints returned session-stored JSON strings with a text/html content type. A browser receiving such a response will parse and render the body as HTML, so any HTML or script embedded in the stored value is executed in the victim's context.

Preconditions: the attacker must be an authenticated user with the ability to create or import case content (notes, MISP attributes) containing specially crafted quote or angle-bracket sequences. The victim must subsequently open the affected case timeline, run a search, or request one of the selection endpoints.

Impact: successful exploitation yields DOM-based cross-site scripting in the victim's browser session, potentially allowing disclosure of case data, session manipulation, or execution of arbitrary actions under the victim's identity.

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

flowintel contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrative users to access sensitive configuration data and logs intended for administrators only.

The notification page and alert API responses exposed sensitive fields, including webhook URLs, signing secrets, IMAP credentials, and delivery logs, in the initial data or JSON responses. Although the user interface hid the configuration form from non-admin users, the underlying data remained accessible via the page source or API endpoints. This exposure included historical webhook URLs that may contain active bearer tokens.

An attacker with a valid non-admin account could retrieve these credentials and logs, potentially leading to unauthorized access to notification services, impersonation of the application in webhook deliveries, or further lateral movement within the infrastructure.

Affected versions: flowintel < 4.1.0

flowintel contains an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability affecting multiple endpoints that manage child records of cases and tasks. An authenticated user with access to one case or task could read or modify records belonging to other cases by supplying identifiers of those records directly in the request.

Affected operations include:
- Reading task notes, subtasks, and URL tools by referencing their IDs without verifying they belong to the authorized task
- Retrieving task assignees for a task belonging to a different case
- Editing or deleting timeline events and timeline event links belonging to another case
- Editing or removing case connectors belonging to another case
- Invoking connector module operations (MISP, generic connectors, worker calls) by combining an authorized case with a connector link from a different case

The root cause is that the application authorized the parent resource (case or task) in the URL but then fetched or operated on the child record independently without verifying the child's ownership relationship to the authorized parent.

Security impact: an authenticated user can exfiltrate sensitive threat intelligence data from cases they do not have access to, and can modify or delete timeline entries, connector configurations, and other records in unauthorized cases, leading to data integrity loss and potential disruption of incident response workflows.

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0

flowintel contains multiple authorization bypass vulnerabilities in its Analyzer (MISP Modules) functionality, affecting both the web interface and the REST API.

- Saving analyzer results to a case or task accepted caller-supplied case and task identifiers without verifying that the authenticated user is a member of the target case or holds the required restricted-task permissions. An authenticated user could write notes, create tasks, and attach MISP objects or attributes into another organization's case.

- Stored analyzer results were retrievable by UUID by any authenticated user. Both the web endpoint and the API endpoint returned the full result payload without checking ownership, exposing another user's analysis output.

- The save handler did not validate the structure of the request, did not reject conflicting destination selections, and did not halt processing when a task-note operation failed, allowing partial or unintended writes.

Preconditions: the attacker must possess a valid authenticated session (or API token) in flowintel. No administrative role is required.

Security impact: unauthorized cross-tenant data disclosure (analyzer results) and unauthorized cross-tenant data modification (notes, tasks, MISP objects/attributes in another organization's case).

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

FlowIntel contains multiple authorization and credential management vulnerabilities affecting connector instances, MISP helper tools, and case templates.

- Connector instance metadata, connectivity checks, and case listings accepted instance IDs without verifying if the acting user had visibility or ownership rights, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive configuration and data.
- Case template serialization and creation processes exposed connector instances attached to templates regardless of the user's permissions, potentially leaking credentials or instance details to users who should not have access.
- Editing connector instances allowed changes to URLs or sharing scopes without requiring re-authentication of API keys, enabling the reuse of another user's credentials in a new context or the leakage of shared keys to unauthorized endpoints.
- Outbound MISP connector keys were incorrectly accepted for authenticating incoming alerts, bypassing the intended separation between outbound integration credentials and inbound alert source authentication.

These issues allow authenticated users to access unauthorized connector data, manipulate credential scopes, and potentially exploit credential confusion between different security contexts.

Affected versions: < 4.1.0

FlowIntel contains an authorization bypass in its user directory and assignment endpoints that allows authenticated users to access data belonging to other organisations.

When the LIMIT_USER_VIEW_TO_ORG setting is enabled to restrict directory visibility to the caller's organisation, several API endpoints (user lookup by ID, last name, Matrix ID, and role-based listings) did not consistently enforce the organisation boundary. An authenticated non-admin user could retrieve profiles of users in other organisations by supplying their identifiers.

Additionally, OrgAdmin users could retrieve the task assignments of any user in the system, including tasks and case titles from private cases to which they had no access. The assignment endpoints did not verify that the requested user belonged to the caller's organisation or that the underlying cases were visible to the caller.

Security impact:
- Exposure of user identities (names, Matrix IDs, roles) across organisation boundaries
- Disclosure of task assignments, case titles, and workflow details from private cases
- Potential enumeration of other organisations' membership and case activity

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

Flowintel contains multiple SSO identity and organisation trust boundary violations that collectively allow account takeover, privilege escalation, and unauthorized access to private case data.

- Keycloak SSO accepted unverified email claims, and all SSO providers (Keycloak, Entra ID, SimpleSAML) could resolve a claimed email address to an existing account that was created via a different sign-in method, enabling cross-provider account collision and unauthorized access to another user's account and data.

- Entra ID role mapping relied on group display names, which tenant members could duplicate by creating a group with the same name as a privileged group (e.g. FlowintelAdmin), resulting in unauthorized role escalation.

- SSO provisioning reused organisations whose display names matched user-controlled profile names, granting the new SSO user access to that organisation's private cases without explicit administrator assignment.

- Case sharing via the API resolved organisations by name using a first-match query, so ambiguous names could silently resolve to the wrong organisation.

Preconditions: an attacker must have a valid SSO identity (Keycloak, Entra ID, or SimpleSAML) or be a member of the relevant Entra tenant. No local administrator access is required.

Security impact: unauthorized access to private case data, privilege escalation to Editor or higher roles, and account takeover across authentication providers.

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

Flowintel contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in its Matrix relay (bot) integration. When the relay forwarded API requests on behalf of a represented user, the authorization and permission checks evaluated the relay bot's elevated role while the request handlers acted as the lower-privileged represented user. This mismatch allowed users with restricted roles (e.g., Read Only) to perform write operations, directory lookups, calendar modifications, assignment changes, template creation, and import actions they were not authorized to perform.

Additionally, relay authority was determined by matching editable user profile fields (name and email) rather than a protected, non-spoofable identifier. An ordinary user who modified their profile to match the expected bot name could be recognized as the trusted relay, enabling impersonation of the bot and potential access to its elevated privileges.

Preconditions:
- A valid Flowintel user account with a restricted role (e.g., Read Only)
- Access to the Matrix relay integration or the ability to send API requests with the relay's API key and a MATRIX-ID header
- For the impersonation vector: ability to edit one's own profile name fields

Security impact:
- Unauthorized write operations by users with read-only or otherwise restricted permissions
- Potential impersonation of the trusted relay bot by ordinary users
- Bypass of organization-level access controls and role-based restrictions
- Unauthorized modification of cases, tasks, calendar events, templates, and user directory entries

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0

Flowintel , contained a session management vulnerability in its browser authentication mechanism. The session identifier used a bare numeric user ID rather than a credential-bound token, resulting in several related weaknesses:

- Remembered logins (remember-me cookies) remained valid after a user changed their password, allowing an attacker holding a previously issued cookie to retain access indefinitely.
- Server-side session identifiers were not rotated upon login (local, SSO, or remembered), enabling session fixation.
- Self-service email and password changes did not require verification of the current password, permitting an attacker with an active session to modify account credentials without knowledge of the existing password.
- Administrator-initiated password resets did not revoke other browser sessions, invalidate remembered logins, or rotate the affected user's API key.

An attacker who obtained a valid session or remember-me cookie (e.g., through XSS, network interception, or cookie theft) could maintain unauthorized access even after the legitimate user changed their password. Additionally, an attacker with any valid session could change the account's email address or password without knowing the current credentials, effectively taking over the account.

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

FlowIntel contained a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability affecting fourteen web routes that performed destructive or state-changing operations. The affected routes accepted HTTP GET requests in addition to (or instead of) POST, which bypassed the Flask-WTF CSRF token validation that is only enforced on non-GET requests.

The vulnerable operations included:
- Case deletion and case merging
- Organisation removal from a case
- Task deletion (case and template)
- Case template and note template deletion
- Connector, connector instance, and icon deletion
- Custom tag deletion and status change
- Taxonomy and galaxy status changes

An attacker who could induce an authenticated user to follow a crafted link or load a page containing a cross-site navigation (e.g., an image tag or redirect) could trigger any of these destructive actions using the victim's session cookie, without the victim's explicit consent or awareness. No special privileges beyond a valid authenticated session with the appropriate role (editor or admin) were required on the victim's account.

Security impact: unauthorized deletion or modification of cases, tasks, templates, connectors, icons, custom tags, taxonomies, and galaxies belonging to the victim or the organisation, resulting in loss of data integrity.

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

Flowintel disabled TLS certificate verification for all MISP API connections and used unverified SSL contexts for IMAP and SMTP STARTTLS mail connections. This allowed an on-path (man-in-the-middle) attacker positioned between Flowintel and its MISP or mail servers to impersonate the remote server and intercept sensitive data.

Affected connections include:
- All MISP HTTPS API calls (event retrieval, attribute search, event creation, connectivity checks, and API validation)
- SMTP STARTTLS connections used for sending email notifications
- IMAP TLS connections used for fetching mail archives and testing connectivity

An attacker who can observe or intercept network traffic between Flowintel and the MISP or mail server could:
- Capture MISP API keys and mail credentials (SMTP/IMAP passwords)
- Read all threat intelligence data exchanged (events, attributes, objects, reports)
- Inject or modify threat intelligence data returned to Flowintel

The vulnerability required no authentication on the part of the attacker and no user interaction; it was exploitable by any party with a network position between Flowintel and its configured MISP or mail endpoints.

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

FlowIntel contains multiple security flaws in its note variable resolution, chatbot API tooling, and AI report generation.

- Note variable references (e.g. cross-case or cross-task lookups) were resolved using the viewing user's privileges rather than the destination case's audience. An authenticated user with access to a shared or imported note could embed references to private cases, causing sensitive case data to be pulled into AI report requests, exports, and MISP sends without the referenced case's audience having granted read access.

- The chatbot API tool permitted the language model to invoke any FlowIntel API endpoint, including administrative routes and state-changing GET operations, without an allow-list or path validation. An attacker who can influence the model's instructions (e.g. via untrusted case content) could induce data modification or access restricted endpoints.

- AI report generation passed the Ollama bearer token and full case content as command-line arguments to a child process, exposing them in the system process table to any local user.

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0.

The flowintel Docker build workflow used the GitHub Actions checkout action with default credential persistence, causing the job authentication token to be written into the repository's Git configuration file. This file became part of the Docker build context and could be retained in exported build cache layers, even though Git metadata was stripped from the final runtime image.

An attacker with access to the CI/CD build cache or build environment could extract the persisted token and use it to gain unauthorized access to the private source repository.

Impact:
- Exposure of a valid authentication token to the private repository
- Potential unauthorized read access to source code and repository metadata

Affected versions: flowintel < 4.1.0

The Mega Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder with Multi-Step & Conditional Logic plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the delete_entry function in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.9 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). The attacker-supplied path is stored via the unauthenticated form submission endpoint, but the actual file deletion only occurs when an administrator subsequently deletes the stored entry — a routine housekeeping action that serves as the detonation trigger. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Nexter Extension – Security, Performance, Code Snippets & Site Toolkit plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 This is due to the role_switcher_to_view_admin_as() function handling the `reset-view` branch without a capability check or nonce when the caller's own login is supplied, combined with an incomplete cleanup hook (maybe_prevent_switchback_to_administrator) that exits early when the user's current roles equal the stored view role and that is never triggered when WordPress core's WP_User::set_role() short-circuits because the account already has only the target role. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to elevate their privileges to Administrator.

The Mang Board plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion via Path Traversal in versions up to, and including, 2.4.8 via the `file_path` column handled by the `mbw_board_files_api_body()` function. The plugin stores an attacker-supplied value directly into the files admin table (no realpath, dot-segment, or directory-containment filtering) and later concatenates it onto `MBW_UPLOAD_PATH` before passing the result to `@unlink()`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the affected site's server, including `wp-config.

The server processes POST requests to ‘/xmanagercore/api/Project/ConvertBDToProject/’ without verifying the administrative role. An authenticated user with basic privileges can create a project and execute SQL queries on the linked database from that project.

The Pie Register – User Registration, Profiles & Content Restriction plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.4.17 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to overwrite the role of the site's primary administrator account (user ID 1) with the registration form's configured role, demoting the administrator to a lower-privileged role and locking them out of wp-admin. This vulnerability is exploitable only on PHP 8+, where casting a WP_Error object to int yields 1, causing the role modification to target user ID 1.

The CWILL (Formerly ParcelPanel) – Shipment Tracking, Tracking & Order Tracking for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[].courier_code, data[].tracking_number (plus pp_sign for the auth bypass)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.6.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The authentication bypass is reachable only when the parcelpanel_api_key WordPress option is non-empty, which occurs automatically once an admin has opened or connected the ParcelPanel admin page; at that point any unauthenticated attacker can bypass the sole access gate by supplying a JSON boolean true as pp_sign, which PHP's loose == operator coerces to true when compared against the non-empty md5 hex string.

The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event_post (post ID) + event_title (XSS payload) + content (shortcode)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This requires an administrator to have granted the mc_add_events capability to Subscriber-level or other lower-privileged roles, which is the plugin's documented workflow for allowing front-end event submissions.

The Mang Board plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.7. The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event_street' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has granted the mc_add_events capability to Subscriber-level users via the plugin's Permissions settings; once granted, the Subscriber can store the payload without the mc_edit_locations capability because mc_admin_save() does not enforce it before calling mc_insert_location().

The NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 4.5.5 via the 'ajax_pagination_referrer' request parameter used on the /ngg_tag/<tag>/ taxonomy page. This is due to the plugin reading the pagination base URL from $_REQUEST, preserving the attacker-supplied host on the tag route (where ngg_wprouting_add_post_permalink is forced to false so the plugin does not re-base the links to the site's own permalink), and caching the fully rendered page in a transient keyed only on the request URI (not the request body) for 1800 seconds via NGG_RENDERING_CACHE / PHOTOCRATI_CACHE. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to poison the cached /ngg_tag/<tag>/ page so that its pagination links point to an attacker-controlled host; the plugin's own ajax_pagination.

The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'mc_template (template body); event_title (payload storage)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. The Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the plugin's "What must the lightbox be applied to?" setting (thumbEffectContext) to be configured as "Try to apply to all images" or "Try to apply to all images that link to image files," which is not the shipping default, and also requires the attacker's comment to reach a publicly rendered state.

In `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2` versions `<= 2.0.0-rc8` (and the deprecated v1 module paths `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11 <= 1.6.8`, `github.com/ThalesGroup/crypto11 <= 1.7.0-rc1` and `github.com/ThalesIgnite/crypto11 <= 1.2.5`), the key-pair and certificate lookup functions (`FindKeyPair`, `FindKeyPairs`, `FindKeyPairsWithAttributes`, `FindAllKeyPairs`, the `FindRSAKeyPair*` family and `FindAllPairedCertificates`) pair a private key with a public key object, or with a certificate, by `CKA_ID`/`CKA_LABEL` alone, take the first match the token returns, and never verify that it belongs to the private key. PKCS#11 permits a session that has not logged in to create public token objects, so anyone able to open a session on the token — without the PIN — can plant a public key or certificate carrying a victim key's `CKA_ID` and label, and crypto11 may return it as that key's public half. An application that publishes or trusts `Signer.Public()` (a JWKS endpoint, a key registry, `authorized_keys`, a CSR) then publishes the attacker's key, and relying parties accept anything the attacker signs as coming from the service. On the v1 line the lookup also falls back to a class-and-key-type-only search when the private key has no `CKA_ID`, pairing a label-only private key with the first public key of its type on the token.



The v1 module paths are deprecated and will not be fixed; users should migrate to github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2 version 2.0.0-rc9 or later.

flowintel contains a log injection vulnerability in its case history (audit log) subsystem. The case history is stored as a line-delimited file where each line represents a single event attributed to a specific user. User-controlled fields, including user names, event messages, and case titles used during case merging, were written to the history file without sanitizing embedded line separator characters (such as carriage return, line feed, vertical tab, form feed, and Unicode line/paragraph separators).

An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify case history entries could embed line separators in these fields. Upon writing, the injected separators would split a single intended entry into multiple lines, each of which the history format interprets as a distinct event. This allows an attacker to forge additional history entries attributed to arbitrary users, corrupting the audit trail and undermining the integrity of case records.

The vulnerability affects the case history append and merge operations. No authentication bypass or privilege escalation is required beyond normal case-management access.

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

FlowIntel contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its file-to-note conversion feature. When a user converts an attached CSV or JSON file into a case note, the application renders the data as a Markdown table by padding every row to the maximum column count. A crafted file with a small number of filled cells but a very large number of columns (or keys) causes the application to allocate a quadratic number of padded table cells, potentially exhausting a worker process in memory or CPU.

The same issue affects nested JSON values rendered inside table cells, where pretty-printed indentation further inflates the output size.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated user with access to a case in FlowIntel
- Ability to attach and convert a CSV or JSON file to a note

Impact:
- Denial of service: exhaustion of a worker process, potentially disrupting service for other users
- No confidentiality or integrity impact

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

A flaw was found in certmonger. This vulnerability allows a malicious certificate authority or an attacker positioned on an unencrypted network to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending oversized or deliberately slow responses. Certmonger fails to enforce size limits or transfer timeouts when downloading and buffering Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP) replies over HTTP. Consequently, an attacker can exhaust host memory, drive CPU usage to capacity, or cause certificate requests to hang indefinitely.

Flowintel's template repository subsystem did not adequately constrain file access to the configured repository base directory. Two related weaknesses existed:

- Repository registration and editing accepted arbitrary local paths without verifying they resolved inside the configured REPOSITORY_BASE_PATH, allowing an authenticated user to point a repository at any readable directory on the host.
- Manifest and template file lookups used normalized (non-canonical) path joins and a startswith-based guard that could be bypassed by symbolic links, permitting reads of files outside the intended repository.

An authenticated user with the ability to add or edit a template repository could therefore cause the application to read and return the contents of arbitrary files readable by the service account, including configuration files, credentials, or other sensitive data.

Affected: Flowintel versions prior to 4.1.0.

A flaw was found in cluster-network-operator. The OVN IPsec certificate signer does not verify that the requested certificate Subject and DNS names belong to the requesting node. An attacker with an accepted OVN node credential and permission to submit certificate signing requests could obtain a signed certificate identifying another node. In certificate authenticated OVN IPsec deployments, this could enable peer impersonation when the attacker can also satisfy the configured peer address check, potentially compromising protected traffic.

The EU Order Withdrawal Button for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Execution requires an Administrator or Shop Manager to open the Withdrawals Preview modal and click the injected note element, which the attacker can enlarge via a retained style attribute to cover the entire note area. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Chatterbug Forms – Fast, Flexible WordPress Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the cbforms_delete_uploaded_files function in all versions up to, and including, 1.1 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Exploitation requires an administrator to delete the attacker-planted form entry, and the attacker must know or be able to guess the absolute path of a file writable by the PHP process. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

In the nrfconnect/ncs-zigbee repository, the GitHub Actions workflow
.github/workflows/build_documentation.yml used the pull_request_target trigger
while checking out and executing untrusted pull request code. This allowed a
pull request from a fork to run attacker-controlled code in the base repository
context with a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: write, pages: write,
pull-requests: write), enabling remote code execution in CI, token
exfiltration, and unauthorized modification of repository content and GitHub
Pages. The workflow was disabled and then rewritten to remove the issue.

The Events Made Easy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event[event_notes]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is only exploitable when the plugin's 'Allow guest submit?' Frontend Submit option is enabled, though the required nonce is freely obtainable by any anonymous visitor as it is printed on every frontend page.

The FV Flowplayer Video Player plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[videos][0][fv_wp_flowplayer_field_src]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.5.57.7212 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The fv_player_db_save AJAX endpoint's INSERT path is gated only by a per-user preview nonce and never calls current_user_can(), allowing any authenticated subscriber-level user who possesses their own nonce to store the malicious payload. Exploitation by attackers with subscriber-level access and above requires that administrator has enabled the plugin option fvwpflowplayer['profile_videos_enable_bio']=true (off by default), which enqueues the shortcode editor and the per-user preview_nonce on wp-admin/profile.php for every logged-in user. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.

Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic (Cypher injection) in the orderBy placeholder handling for custom queries in Neo4j Spring Data Neo4j versions 6.1.0 through 8.0.8 and 8.1.0 through 8.1.2 allows a remote attacker to read database contents via blind reads, write read content into new nodes, or, if APOC and APOC file export are enabled, to write query results to a file in the database's accessible file system via crafted sort order parameters. Exploitation requires an application that passes unvalidated user input as the orderBy value to a custom Cypher query using the placeholder directive.

The FV Flowplayer Video Player plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.5.57.7212 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the plugin's 'Parse Vimeo and YouTube links' setting to be enabled, which wires do_shortcode into the comment_text filter chain and allows the [fvplayer] shortcode to be rendered from comment content.
